fields: Why is “good responses” an inadequate evaluation goal?
It is not operationally defined or measurable against a threshold.
What dimensions should an AI system evaluation consider?
Task quality plus relevant latency, cost, safety, security, and business outcomes.
Why can a single aggregate score be misleading?
A system can pass overall while failing important safety, subgroup, or tail-latency constraints.
What should an eval suite represent?
The real workload, important edge cases, historical failures, adversarial cases, and multi-turn behavior where relevant.
When is a deterministic grader preferable to an LLM judge?
When correctness can be checked exactly with code, schema, tests, or external state.
Why run repeated trials for some agent tasks?
Model/agent behavior can be stochastic, so one run may not characterize reliability.
What should an A/B test begin with?
A specific hypothesis and pre-defined primary and guardrail metrics.
What is shadow testing?
Running a candidate on real traffic without allowing its outputs to affect users or production state.
What is the key diagnostic principle for AI systems?
Identify and fix the layer causing the failure rather than masking it downstream.
Why is “hallucination” an incomplete diagnosis?
Wrong output can originate from retrieval, tools, orchestration, stale data, model mismatch, or prompting.
What should optimization minimize?
Resource use per successful outcome while preserving required quality, safety, and reliability.
How can context engineering reduce cost?
Remove low-value context, use just-in-time retrieval/compaction, and avoid repeatedly sending unnecessary data.
Why must evaluation continue after launch?
Real traffic, dependencies, models, and data distributions change over time.
What is a regression eval?
A test that checks known-good behavior still works after changes.
Outcome metric
A measure of whether the task produced the desired real-world result.
Guardrail metric
A secondary threshold that must not regress while optimizing a primary metric.
Trial
One execution of an evaluation task.
Grader
The mechanism that scores whether a task/run met defined criteria.
Control
The baseline experience/system in a controlled experiment.
Treatment
The candidate change being tested against the control.
Retrieval failure
The relevant evidence is not retrieved or is outranked by wrong evidence.
Orchestration failure
Correct components are coordinated incorrectly, such as dropped worker results or wrong ordering.
Cost per successful outcome
Total resource cost divided by tasks that actually meet the success criteria.
Prompt caching
Reusing eligible stable prompt/context content rather than recomputing/sending it as uncached work each time.
Capability eval
An evaluation asking whether the system can perform a new or harder capability.
A useful metric needs a definition, a measurement method, and an {{c1::acceptance threshold}}.
Agent evaluation should include {{c1::external outcomes}} when model claims alone are insufficient.
Multi-dimensional systems should not be reduced to a single vague {{c1::accuracy score}}.
Use the {{c1::cheapest reliable grader}} that can accurately measure the property of interest.
For agents, inspect both final {{c1::outcomes and trajectories}} when intermediate behavior matters.
An A/B experiment should define the hypothesis, primary metric, guardrails, assignment, and {{c1::decision/stopping rule}} before interpreting results.
{{c1::Shadow testing}} uses real traffic while preventing candidate outputs from affecting production behavior.
Diagnose from {{c1::symptom → evidence → failing stage → targeted fix}}, rather than rewriting prompts blindly.
A fixed production failure should become a {{c1::regression case}}.
Optimize {{c1::cost per successful outcome}}, not just cost per request.
Removing tokens is useful only if required {{c1::quality and safety thresholds}} still pass.
Production monitoring reveals whether the {{c1::real workload or dependencies}} are drifting from assumptions.
Known failures should be converted into {{c1::regression tests/evals}} after remediation.
What term describes a threshold metric that must not regress during optimization?
Guardrail metric
What should define the minimum acceptable value for a metric?
Acceptance threshold
What evaluation component scores a task result?
Grader
What term describes one execution of an eval task?
Trial
What experiment mode runs a candidate on real traffic without exposing users to its outputs?
Shadow testing
What is the baseline arm of an A/B experiment called?
Control
What failure class occurs when relevant evidence never reaches the model?
Retrieval failure
What failure class occurs when correct components are sequenced or coordinated incorrectly?
Orchestration failure
What efficiency metric accounts for failures/retries rather than only request price?
Cost per successful outcome
What evaluation protects known-good behavior from breaking after changes?
Regression evaluation
A team says its support agent is “very accurate.” What should an architect request next?

[{"id":"a","text":"A defined metric, representative measurement method, and acceptance threshold."},{"id":"b","text":"A longer system prompt."},{"id":"c","text":"A larger context window."},{"id":"d","text":"More agents."}]
a
Evaluation claims must be operationalized.
A candidate model improves task success but doubles safety-policy violations. What should the team conclude?

[{"id":"a","text":"The candidate fails a critical guardrail even if the primary quality metric improved."},{"id":"b","text":"Ship it because primary accuracy is higher."},{"id":"c","text":"Ignore safety because it is hard to score."},{"id":"d","text":"Average the two metrics into one number and accept any positive result."}]
a
Safety/security floors can constrain optimization.
A coding agent says it fixed a bug, but tests still fail. What is the stronger evaluation metric?

[{"id":"a","text":"The external task outcome, such as passing the relevant tests."},{"id":"b","text":"The agent's confidence."},{"id":"c","text":"Length of the explanation."},{"id":"d","text":"Number of tool calls."}]
a
External outcome can be more authoritative than model claims.
Which metric best represents user-facing responsiveness when occasional slow requests matter?

[{"id":"a","text":"A tail-latency percentile such as p95, paired with an SLA threshold."},{"id":"b","text":"Only average latency."},{"id":"c","text":"Total tokens ever used."},{"id":"d","text":"Number of prompt lines."}]
a
Tail latency matters when a minority of very slow requests harm the experience.
A tool action should create exactly one database row. What is the best grader?

[{"id":"a","text":"A deterministic check of the database state."},{"id":"b","text":"An LLM judge reading the agent's explanation."},{"id":"c","text":"A human reviewer for every run."},{"id":"d","text":"The model's self-reported success."}]
a
Exact external state should be verified deterministically.
A style rubric is nuanced and cannot be checked with simple code. What grader may be appropriate after calibration?

[{"id":"a","text":"A model-based grader evaluated against human-labeled examples."},{"id":"b","text":"A schema validator only."},{"id":"c","text":"A random score."},{"id":"d","text":"No grader at all."}]
a
Model graders can score nuanced qualities but should be calibrated.
An eval suite contains only easy happy-path requests. What is the biggest weakness?

[{"id":"a","text":"It may miss boundary, adversarial, malformed, and historical failure modes."},{"id":"b","text":"It contains too many tasks."},{"id":"c","text":"It should use only one trial."},{"id":"d","text":"It should never include production failures."}]
a
Representative coverage includes important failures, not just routine cases.
An agent's performance varies significantly between runs of the same task. What should the eval framework add?

[{"id":"a","text":"Multiple trials per task to measure reliability under stochastic behavior."},{"id":"b","text":"One carefully chosen run only."},{"id":"c","text":"A longer deck name."},{"id":"d","text":"Fewer measurements."}]
a
Repeated trials characterize variance.
A team changes the model, prompt, retriever, and tool schema simultaneously, then sees improvement. What is the main problem?

[{"id":"a","text":"The experiment cannot attribute the change because several major variables moved together."},{"id":"b","text":"A/B testing requires more than two models."},{"id":"c","text":"All variables should always change together."},{"id":"d","text":"Guardrail metrics are unnecessary."}]
a
Controlled experiments isolate specific hypotheses.
A new agent can execute risky production writes. How can the team first test it on realistic traffic without exposing users to its actions?

[{"id":"a","text":"Use shadow testing with outputs/actions prevented from affecting production."},{"id":"b","text":"Turn it on for every user immediately."},{"id":"c","text":"Disable logging."},{"id":"d","text":"Use only a synthetic prompt unrelated to production."}]
a
Shadow testing provides realistic input without direct production effect.
A treatment improves accuracy by 0.05% with strong statistical significance but adds major cost. What should the architect consider?

[{"id":"a","text":"Whether the improvement is practically valuable enough to justify the cost."},{"id":"b","text":"Statistical significance guarantees business value."},{"id":"c","text":"Ignore cost once p<0.05."},{"id":"d","text":"Always ship any measurable improvement."}]
a
Practical significance and guardrails matter.
An experiment's primary quality metric rises while latency breaches the SLA. What should happen?

[{"id":"a","text":"Treat the latency SLA as a guardrail and reject or revise the treatment."},{"id":"b","text":"Ship because primary quality improved."},{"id":"c","text":"Remove the SLA from reporting."},{"id":"d","text":"Average quality and latency into one unbounded score."}]
a
Guardrails prevent one metric from improving by violating another requirement.
A model gives wrong answers because the retriever returns obsolete documents. What should change first?

[{"id":"a","text":"Fix the retrieval freshness/ranking problem."},{"id":"b","text":"Add more system-prompt warnings."},{"id":"c","text":"Upgrade the model without inspecting retrieval."},{"id":"d","text":"Retry the same stale evidence."}]
a
The failing layer is retrieval, not necessarily prompting.
A tool returns malformed JSON and the agent fails. What is the most direct diagnosis?
[{"id":"a","text":"Tool/interface contract failure."},{"id":"b","text":"Hallucination by definition."},{"id":"c","text":"Model lifecycle failure."},{"id":"d","text":"Business-value failure."}]
a
Inspect the interface actually producing the malformed data.
A worker computes the correct result, but the orchestrator drops it before synthesis. What failure class is this?
[{"id":"a","text":"Orchestration failure."},{"id":"b","text":"Retrieval failure."},{"id":"c","text":"Prompt injection."},{"id":"d","text":"Model deprecation."}]
a
The component result is correct; coordination is wrong.
After repairing a recurrent production failure, what should the team add?

[{"id":"a","text":"A regression test/eval reproducing the failure so it stays fixed."},{"id":"b","text":"Remove observability."},{"id":"c","text":"Delete historical evidence."},{"id":"d","text":"Only document that someone remembers the fix."}]
a
Known failures should become protected regression cases.
A cheaper model causes twice as many retries and escalations. What metric should decide whether it is actually cheaper?

[{"id":"a","text":"Cost per successful outcome including retries/escalations."},{"id":"b","text":"Price per single API call only."},{"id":"c","text":"Model name length."},{"id":"d","text":"Prompt token count alone."}]
a
A cheap failing request can raise total cost.
Tool results contain 100,000 rows but the model needs only an aggregate. What is a strong optimization?

[{"id":"a","text":"Process/filter the data programmatically and pass only the high-signal result to the model."},{"id":"b","text":"Send every row through multiple model turns."},{"id":"c","text":"Duplicate the rows in the system prompt."},{"id":"d","text":"Disable the tool."}]
a
Programmatic processing reduces token/context overhead.
A prompt includes large historical logs that never affect decisions. What should the team test?

[{"id":"a","text":"Remove or compact low-value context and confirm quality still passes."},{"id":"b","text":"Add more logs to improve cost."},{"id":"c","text":"Increase output length."},{"id":"d","text":"Use the strongest model only."}]
a
Low-value context wastes tokens and may harm relevance.
An optimization removes a safety validation step and lowers p95 latency. Is it acceptable?

[{"id":"a","text":"Only if the validation was not required; required safety controls must remain even when they cost latency."},{"id":"b","text":"Yes, lower latency always dominates."},{"id":"c","text":"Yes, if average accuracy rises."},{"id":"d","text":"Yes, if the model promises to self-check."}]
a
Optimization is constrained by required safety/security thresholds.
Offline evals pass, but tool failures spike after launch because an external API changed. What caught this?

[{"id":"a","text":"Production monitoring of real dependencies and outcomes."},{"id":"b","text":"A static benchmark alone."},{"id":"c","text":"The system prompt."},{"id":"d","text":"A one-time prelaunch demo."}]
a
Production monitoring detects real-world changes offline suites may not predict.
A new model version is deployed. What should protect known behavior?

[{"id":"a","text":"Run the regression suite and monitor production after migration."},{"id":"b","text":"Assume newer means identical."},{"id":"c","text":"Delete old evals."},{"id":"d","text":"Only compare price."}]
a
Model changes can alter behavior and require regression testing.
Users report a novel failure pattern. What should happen after root cause is fixed?

[{"id":"a","text":"Add representative cases to the regression suite and monitor the corrected behavior."},{"id":"b","text":"Ignore it because launch evals already passed."},{"id":"c","text":"Remove the complaint from logs."},{"id":"d","text":"Only increase model temperature."}]
a
Production failures improve future evaluation coverage.
An alert fires but no team owns the metric or runbook. What is missing?
[{"id":"a","text":"Operational ownership and a defined response action."},{"id":"b","text":"Another model."},{"id":"c","text":"More prompt examples."},{"id":"d","text":"A second vector database."}]
a
Monitoring without action/ownership does not close the loop.
Which TWO practices best support defining evaluation metrics?

[{"id":"a","text":"Define measurable thresholds before evaluation."},{"id":"b","text":"Use one vague “accuracy” number for everything."},{"id":"c","text":"Measure external outcomes where possible."},{"id":"d","text":"Ignore tail behavior."}]
Correct: Define measurable thresholds before evaluation.; Measure external outcomes where possible.. The other choices conflict with the approved guidance.

[{"id":"a","text":"Measure external outcomes where possible."},{"id":"b","text":"Optimize only the easiest metric."},{"id":"c","text":"Use multiple metrics for multi-dimensional success."},{"id":"d","text":"Declare success without a threshold."}]
Correct: Measure external outcomes where possible.; Use multiple metrics for multi-dimensional success.. The other choices conflict with the approved guidance.

Order a metric-definition workflow.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Define the desired outcome"},{"id":"s2","text":"Choose observable measures"},{"id":"s3","text":"Specify how each measure is computed"},{"id":"s4","text":"Set acceptance and guardrail thresholds"},{"id":"s5","text":"Run representative evaluation and compare to thresholds"}]
Metrics become useful only after outcome, measurement, and thresholds are explicit.
Order a basic evaluation-framework design.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Define representative tasks"},{"id":"s2","text":"Choose appropriate graders"},{"id":"s3","text":"Run one or more trials"},{"id":"s4","text":"Collect trajectories/outcomes"},{"id":"s5","text":"Aggregate results against thresholds"}]
Task definition and grading come before execution and aggregation.
Order a controlled improvement experiment.

[{"id":"s1","text":"State the hypothesis"},{"id":"s2","text":"Choose primary and guardrail metrics"},{"id":"s3","text":"Define assignment and decision rule"},{"id":"s4","text":"Run control/treatment or shadow evaluation"},{"id":"s5","text":"Analyze results and decide whether to ship"}]
Pre-specification precedes execution and interpretation.
Order a root-cause diagnostic loop.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Reproduce the symptom"},{"id":"s2","text":"Inspect trace/outcome evidence"},{"id":"s3","text":"Identify the likely failing stage"},{"id":"s4","text":"Run a targeted isolation test"},{"id":"s5","text":"Apply the fix and add regression coverage"}]

Order a safe optimization cycle.

[{"id":"s1","text":"Measure baseline quality, latency, and cost"},{"id":"s2","text":"Identify the dominant resource driver"},{"id":"s3","text":"Apply one targeted optimization"},{"id":"s4","text":"Re-run quality/safety/latency evals"},{"id":"s5","text":"Keep the change only if all required thresholds pass"}]

Order a production learning loop.
